newsitem.title: USA: Appeals court keeps bombing case papers sealed.
newsitem.headline: Appeals court keeps bombing case papers sealed.

text.p: A federal appeals court in Denver turned down Monday a news media request to unseal key documents in the Oklahoma City bombing case.
The 10th Circuit Court of Appeals said federal trial Judge Richard Matsch properly sealed the documents to ensure fair trials for defendants Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols.
A jury last month convicted McVeigh of the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building that killed 168 people and sentenced him to die. Nichols' trial is to begin Sept. 29.
-- A Federal Bureau of Investigation report of nine hours of statements Nichols made to agents two days after the bombing.
-- Portions of the defendants' requests for separate trials, which the court said included the defendants' attempts to blame each other for the bombing.

-- Portions of Nichols' motion to suppress evidence. The court said the sealed portions were limited to material that Matsch ruled was inadmissible in McVeigh's trial. Matsch ruled that Nichols' statements to the FBI could not be admitted as evidence in McVeigh's trial.
